questions.q: Which argument of RandomizedSearchCV sets how many hyperparameter combinations are sampled?
questions.explain: n_iter is the number of sampled combinations. The total number of fits is n_iter times the number of folds.

questions.q: Why is random search often more efficient than grid search when there are many hyperparameters?
options: It always finds the global optimum
You control the budget with n_iter, and it can try many distinct values of each hyperparameter
It only works with tree models
questions.explain: A grid repeats the same few values of each hyperparameter, while random draws explore many distinct values under a fixed budget.

questions.q: For a hyperparameter like C that may range from 0.001 to 100, which distribution suits random search best?
options: A list containing only the number 1
questions.explain: loguniform samples evenly across orders of magnitude, so small values get as much attention as large ones.

questions.q: What does Bayesian hyperparameter optimization do differently from random search?
options: It uses the scores of earlier trials to choose the next settings to try
It tests every combination in a grid
It trains only on the test set
questions.explain: Bayesian methods build a cheap model of score versus settings from past trials and use it to pick promising next trials.

questions.q: In the lesson, the random search used n_iter=20 with cv=5. About how many model fits ran during the search?
questions.explain: 20 sampled combinations times 5 folds gives 100 fits, compared with 340,200 combinations in a full grid over the same ranges.
